title: _run.json - the run record
description: Written by src/run/run_matsim.py on a successful run, and ONLY on a successful run: its presence is what makes a run resumable, and a run that died leaves none. Everything needed to identify and repeat the run.

name.description: Run directory name; the run identity.

scenario.description: Validated against the CITY'S OWN declared intervention.scenarios at write time (src/registry/outputs.py injects the enum from city.json; issue #62 A1) - the portable schema file itself names no city's vocabulary.

day.description: Validated against the CITY'S OWN declared day_types at write time (src/registry/outputs.py injects the enum from city.json; issue #62 A1) - the portable schema file itself names no city's vocabulary.

fraction.description: Sample fraction. Every extensive quantity below is scaled by it.

threads.description: PART OF THE RUN IDENTITY, not a performance knob: MATSim partitions the network by thread count, so two runs that differ only here are not the same run.

overrides.description: Config overrides applied to this run.

config_snapshot.description: Relative path to the resolved registry snapshot for this run. A result without one cannot state what inputs produced it.

transit_capacity_scaled.description: Per vehicle type: [attribute, before, after]. Empty at fraction 1.0. Seats MUST scale with the sample or a 10% run gives every bus ten times its real capacity and crowding silently disappears.

controler_sha256.description: sha256 over the committed source of src/java/citysim, the MATSim entry point this run executed. The run name is built from the scenario and the registry values and cannot see the controler, so without this a result produced before a controler change and one produced after would share a name and be indistinguishable. run_matsim.py refuses to resume a completed run whose recorded hash differs from the current source. Absent from records written before DECISIONS.md 9.26.

inputs_sha256.description: sha256 of the day's population file the run sampled from (DECISIONS.md 9.127): part of the run's identity, so a rebuilt demand under the same parameters is a different run and cannot resume an earlier one; null when the file was absent.

warm_started_from.description: Present only on a warm-started run (issue #75): the dead parent run and the plans checkpoint iteration this run continued from. A warm-started run is NOT bit-identical to an uninterrupted one (DECISIONS.md 9.76), so this key is part of run identity and resume matching.
